audits.title: Multicentre audit of inpatient management of acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: comparison with clinical guidelines.
audits.standard: Clinical guidelines for COPD exacerbation management
audits.setting: Eight acute-care hospitals in Hunter New England region

cycle1.result: Spirometry performed in 34% of admissions (inter-hospital range 4-58%).

audits.other_findings: Mean length of stay 6.3 days; wide inter-hospital variation in best practice provision.
audits.citation: Pretto JJ, McDonald VM, Wark PA, Hensley MJ. Multicentre audit of inpatient management of acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: comparison with clinical guidelines. Intern Med J. 2012;42(4):380-387. doi:10.1111/j.1445-5994.2011.02475.x. PMID: 21395962.

audits.title: Changes in NHS organization of care and management of hospital admissions with COPD exacerbations between the national COPD audits of 2003 and 2008.
audits.standard: National COPD audit processes of care and organisation of care
audits.setting: 192 UK acute hospital units, national COPD audits 2003 and 2008

cycle1.result: 2003 national COPD audit baseline (up to 60 consecutive admissions per unit); detailed figures not stated in abstract.

audits.intervention: Improvements in resources and organisation of care between audit rounds

cycle2.result: Adjusted inpatient mortality (P = 0.05) and 90-day mortality (P = 0.001) reduced; more patients discharged under a respiratory specialist.

audits.other_findings: Considerable variation in quality of secondary care between units persisted.
audits.citation: George PM, Stone RA, Buckingham RJ, Pursey NA, Lowe D, Roberts CM. Changes in NHS organization of care and management of hospital admissions with COPD exacerbations between the national COPD audits of 2003 and 2008. QJM. 2011;104(10):859-866. doi:10.1093/qjmed/hcr083. PMID: 21622541.

audits.title: Clinical audit of COPD patients requiring hospital admissions in Spain: AUDIPOC study.
audits.setting: 129 Spanish hospitals covering 70% of the population

cycle1.result: Median inpatient mortality 5% (range 0-35%); 37% readmitted and 6.5% died after discharge; overall mortality 11.6%. Management mostly complied with diagnosis and treatment recommendations.

audits.other_findings: Wide variability between hospitals in resources, adherence to guidelines and outcomes.
audits.citation: Pozo-Rodríguez F, López-Campos JL, Alvarez-Martínez CJ, Castro-Acosta A, Agüero R, Hueto J, et al.. Clinical audit of COPD patients requiring hospital admissions in Spain: AUDIPOC study. PLoS One. 2012;7(7):e42156. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0042156. PMID: 22911875.

audits.title: European hospital adherence to GOLD recommendations for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation admissions.

cycle1.result: Adherence to the 10 key recommendations varied between hospitals and countries (no figures given in abstract).

audits.other_findings: Lack of available spirometry and variable use of oxygen and NIV were high-impact areas for improvement.

audits.title: Variability of hospital resources for acute care of COPD patients: the European COPD Audit.
audits.setting: 425 hospitals from 13 national societies, European COPD Audit

cycle1.result: Larger hospitals had more resources and staff; guideline adherence varied with hospital size but differences were small and inconsistent.

audits.other_findings: Mean beds per tertile 220, 479 and 989; more resources did not always mean better care.
audits.citation: López-Campos JL, Hartl S, Pozo-Rodriguez F, Roberts CM, European COPD Audit team. Variability of hospital resources for acute care of COPD patients: the European COPD Audit. Eur Respir J. 2014;43(3):754-762. doi:10.1183/09031936.00074413. PMID: 23988775.

audits.title: Results from an audit feedback strategy for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in-hospital care: a joint analysis from the AUDIPOC and European COPD audit studies.
audits.standard: Clinical care standards for COPD exacerbation admissions
audits.setting: 94 hospitals in Spain (AUDIPOC and European COPD audit)

cycle1.result: Initial clinical care reasonably acceptable with considerable variability.

audits.intervention: Personalised reports to each centre, presentation and discussion of results at regional, national and international meetings, and creation of COPD healthcare quality standards.

cycle2.result: Several diagnostic and therapeutic procedures improved; improvements significant but small to moderate.

audits.citation: Lopez-Campos JL, Asensio-Cruz MI, Castro-Acosta A, Calero C, Pozo-Rodriguez F, AUDIPOC and the European COPD Audit studies. Results from an audit feedback strategy for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in-hospital care: a joint analysis from the AUDIPOC and European COPD audit studies. PLoS One. 2014;9(10):e110394. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0110394. PMID: 25333953.

audits.title: Improving the acute care of COPD patients across Gloucestershire: a quality improvement project.
audits.standard: BTS COPD admission care bundle and local CQUIN target

cycle1.result: 63% received all bundle elements (up from 10% before bundle paperwork was introduced in June 2014)

audits.intervention: Focus group of junior medical staff to raise awareness, following introduction of bundle paperwork with training

cycle2.result: 73% received all elements of the bundle; steroids and antibiotics within four hours 96%; appropriate oxygen prescription 87% (from 97%)

audits.other_findings: Blood gas analysis, nebuliser use and respiratory review improved; oxygen prescription declined.
audits.citation: Miller C, Cushley C, Redler K, Mitchell C, Aynsley Day E, Mansfield H, et al.. Improving the acute care of COPD patients across Gloucestershire: a quality improvement project. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u208427.w3338. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u208427.w3338. PMID: 26734406.

audits.title: The European COPD audit : Adherence to guidelines, readmission risk and hospital care for acute exacerbations in Austria.
audits.standard: International COPD guidelines for acute exacerbation care
audits.setting: 26 hospitals in Austria (specialised respiratory vs general care), European COPD audit

cycle1.result: Adherence to blood gas analysis and non-invasive ventilation guidance was greater in specialised respiratory care (figures truncated in abstract).

audits.other_findings: Patients in specialised respiratory care had lower readmission risk; general care patients had more comorbidity.

audits.title: National clinical audit for hospitalised exacerbations of COPD.
audits.standard: National COPD process indicators and standards
audits.setting: UK national COPD audit programme (Royal College of Physicians), hospitals admitting COPD exacerbations

cycle1.result: Length of stay halved from 8 to 4 days between 1997 and 2014; process indicators did not generally improve with sequential cross-sectional audit.

audits.intervention: Continuous audit from 2017 with quality improvement support and financial incentives for some indicators.

cycle2.result: Early specialist review 55-66% and discharge bundle 53-74% (incentivised) improved faster than spirometry availability 40-46% and timely NIV 21-24%.

audits.other_findings: 96% of eligible units took part in cross-sectional audit and 86% in the latest continuous round.
audits.citation: Hurst JR, Quint JK, Stone RA, Silove Y, Youde J, Roberts CM. National clinical audit for hospitalised exacerbations of COPD. ERJ Open Res. 2020;6(3):208-2020. doi:10.1183/23120541.00208-2020. PMID: 32984418.

audits.title: Rapid Implementation of Guideline-Based Care for Acute Exacerbations of COPD in a Low-Resource Setting: An Improvement Brief.
audits.standard: GOLD and NICE guidelines for acute exacerbations of COPD

cycle1.result: Corticosteroids 54%; appropriate antibiotics 62%; smoking cessation counselling 22%; spirometry ordered 18%; discharge planning documented 40%.

audits.intervention: Six-week rapid-cycle intervention: EHR-embedded prompts, education sessions for doctors and nurses, and pocket guides.

cycle2.result: Corticosteroids 88%; appropriate antibiotics 90%; smoking cessation counselling 74%; spirometry 52%; discharge planning 82%.

audits.citation: Saqib M. Rapid Implementation of Guideline-Based Care for Acute Exacerbations of COPD in a Low-Resource Setting: An Improvement Brief. Jt Comm J Qual Patient Saf. 2026;52(2):102-104. doi:10.1016/j.jcjq.2025.11.004. PMID: 41390271.

audits.title: An audit of the assessment and management of patients admitted to Christchurch Hospital with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
audits.setting: Christchurch Hospital, respiratory and general medicine

cycle1.result: Level of consciousness not commented on in 50% and hyperinflation in 40%; oxygen given in 87% but not prescribed in one third; peak flow on admission 74%; arterial blood gas 81%; no discharge summary in 29%.

audits.intervention: Hospital-wide COPD guidelines to be developed
audits.other_findings: Pulse oximetry in place of blood gases missed ventilatory failure in five cases; sedatives given inappropriately in six cases.
audits.citation: Neill AM, Epton MJ, Martin IR, Drennan CJ, Town GI. An audit of the assessment and management of patients admitted to Christchurch Hospital with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. N Z Med J. 1994;107(986 Pt 1):365-367. PMID: 7936461.
